info.title: host/session/v1/session.proto
info.description:
The session interface, at the browser edge: a person signs in and the host
opens a session, and a page's runtime asks who the bearer a request carries is.
The local authority signs in fixture people; the host signs in real ones. A
module never calls this: it is called through the hop.

get.summary:
Current answers the session the caller's bearer (`authorization: Bearer
<bearer>`) belongs to: who a page's request is for, decided by the host,
never read from a header the request wrote. The bearer itself is not
handed back. An unknown, ended or expired session is unauthenticated.

ListCastableTeams answers the teams of the organisation the caller is
signed into that the caller may act as now, each with what it holds, so a
page offers the choice OpenTeamCast decides: listed by OpenTeamCast's one
rule (a team whose roles the caller could grant, member of it or not), and
a team it would refuse is not listed, a team granted nothing included. A
cast answers the one team it acts as. Listing opens nothing: each
OpenTeamCast is decided again when it is asked. The callers OpenTeamCast
refuses are refused here.

ListFixturePeople answers who this authority signs in by fixture token, for
the browser edge's sign-in page: the people are defined once, in the
authority's fixture. A host that signs real people in through its identity
provider has no fixture people and answers none.

post.summary:
AddFixtureTeamMember puts a person in a team, on a host run on its
fixture: what a scenario does to a fixture's directory, where a product
calls the host's own team administration. The caller's bearer is the
session of a person who administers the organisation they are signed
into, and that organisation is the one changed: the team is a team of it
and the person a person of it, or the call is not found. From the next
decision the person holds what the team is granted. Adding a member
twice changes nothing. A cast, a role view and the callers OpenRoleView
refuses are refused here, and so is a person who does not administer the
organisation. A host that was not started on a fixture in a local run
answers a failed precondition, as ListFixturePeople does; a host that
signs real people in does not serve it.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: The team, of the organisation the caller is signed into.

delete.summary:
RemoveFixtureTeamMember takes a person out of a team, on a host run on
its fixture, under AddFixtureTeamMember's rules for who may call and what
is named. From the next decision the person holds nothing through the
team: every Work Context issued to them through a role granted to it is
refused when it is checked, a session cast onto it for them is issued
nothing more, and what they hold otherwise is issued again, freshly.
Removing a person who is no member changes nothing.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: The team, of the organisation the caller is signed into.

parameters.name: personId
parameters.description: The person, of the same organisation.

post.summary:
End ends the session the caller's bearer belongs to, and with it every
session opened from it: its role views and casts, and theirs. From then on
each of those bearers is unauthenticated wherever a session is read:
Current, a person's Issue, and every call here. It is a sign-out, and the
way back from a cast: a browser edge ends the cast it leaves, and the
session the cast was opened from is untouched. Ending is never undone, and
a bearer that names no open session is unauthenticated, as it is anywhere.
A Work Context issued to the session before it ended lapses on its own
expiry. The callers OpenRoleView refuses are refused here.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: EndRequest ends the caller's own session; the bearer is the call's.

post.summary:
OpenRoleView opens a session that acts as some of the roles the caller
holds on one installation: a role view. The caller's bearer is the session
it is opened from. The host records the view, decided by the authority, as
the session's own; a client never supplies it. A view only narrows: it names
roles the calling session acts as now, so a viewing session opens only
narrower ones, and a role view on one installation reaches no other. The
session it was opened from is untouched and stays the way back to all of the
person's roles. A page, a Work Context, an impersonated session and a
client's delegated credential hold no session of a person to call from and
are refused.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: OpenRoleViewRequest names the installation and the roles to act as on it.

post.summary:
OpenTeamCast opens a session that acts as a member of one team and of
nothing else: a cast. It holds that team's grants and none of the caller's
own: no direct grant, no other team, no organisation role, no platform
role, so it answers what a member of the team sees. The caller's bearer is
the session it is opened from. The authority decides, by one rule: a person
may act as a team whose roles they could grant, member of it or not. A team
that holds roles the caller could not grant is refused saying so, and a
team granted nothing is not found, because there is nothing to act as. A
cast is never changed or widened, and a session that is already a cast
opens no other; a role view opened from it stays in it. The session it was
opened from is untouched and is the way back. The callers OpenRoleView
refuses are refused here.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: OpenTeamCastRequest names the team to act as.

post.summary: SignIn opens a session for a fixture person by their fixture token.

personId.description: The person, of the same organisation.

SessionServiceAddFixtureTeamMemberBody.description: AddFixtureTeamMemberRequest names the team and the person to put in it.

v1AddFixtureTeamMemberResponse.description: AddFixtureTeamMemberResponse says the person is a member of the team.

displayName.description:
The team's name, as the host spells it, for a page that offers the
choice; the id above is the identity. A host that names teams by their
id answers the id.

holds.description:
Each role granted to the team on an active installation, by installation
then role.

v1CastableTeam.description: CastableTeam is one team a caller may act as, and what a cast onto it holds.

v1EndRequest.description: EndRequest ends the caller's own session; the bearer is the call's.

v1EndResponse.description: EndResponse says the session and every session opened from it ended.

roles.description: The roles they hold in it.

fixtureToken.description: The token SignIn takes for them.

organizationDisplayName.description:
The organisation's name, as the fixture spells it, for a page that shows
a person where they sign into; the id above is the identity.

v1FixturePerson.description: FixturePerson is one person a fixture run signs in.

v1ListCastableTeamsResponse.description: ListCastableTeamsResponse is every team the caller may act as, by team id.

v1ListFixturePeopleResponse.description: ListFixturePeopleResponse is every fixture person, in the fixture's order.

installationId.description: The installation, of the organisation the caller is signed into.

roles.description: The roles to act as, each one the caller acts as on it now; at least one.

v1OpenRoleViewRequest.description: OpenRoleViewRequest names the installation and the roles to act as on it.

teamId.description: The team, of the organisation the caller is signed into.

v1OpenTeamCastRequest.description: OpenTeamCastRequest names the team to act as.

v1RemoveFixtureTeamMemberResponse.description: RemoveFixtureTeamMemberResponse says the person is no member of the team.

roles.description: The roles acted as there, sorted.

v1RoleViewEntry.description: RoleViewEntry is the roles a session acts as on one installation.

sessionId.description: The session id a person-owned Issue names.

bearer.description:
The credential the person presents on every call as `authorization: Bearer
<bearer>`; whatever this implementation authenticates a person by. The local
authority hands back the session id; the host hands back its access token.

personDisplayName.description: The person's display name, for the browser session surface.

roleView.description:
The role view this session was opened with, by installation: it acts as
these roles there and as every role it holds elsewhere. Empty for a session
that is not a role view.

castTeamId.description:
The team this session was cast onto: it acts as a member of that team and
of nothing else, so `roles` is empty and `team_ids` names this team alone.
Empty for a session that is not a cast.

expiresAtUnix.description:
When the session ends on its own, in Unix seconds: from then on its bearer
is unauthenticated wherever a session is read, as an ended one is. Every
session carries one. A role view or a cast ends no later than the session
it was opened from. A browser edge keeps its cookie no longer than this.

grantEpoch.description:
The grant epoch of who this session acts as: a value that is different
whenever what the session holds on the organisation's installations is
different, so it moves when a role is granted or revoked, to the person,
to a team of theirs or to the team a cast acts as, when they leave a team,
and when an installation is made, upgraded or ended. It is opaque and is
compared for equality only. A caller that keeps a Work Context it was
issued for this session (a browser edge) reads it on Current and drops
what it keeps when it differs, so a change made anywhere applies from the
next call instead of when the kept context lapses. Empty: the host states
none, and the caller keeps what it holds until it lapses or is refused.

target.description: What it installs, as the installation names it.

v1TeamHolding.description: TeamHolding is one role a team holds on one installation.
